answer: Nobody is waved through free: £55 in fees and a 10-day delay before the stamp dries is the price, and the voyage never covers it twice. The ledger counts names, not wishes, and every name on it has paid its own way. The desk only stamps a name that carries Diebound press auditor shank charter, and the stamp itself rests on a charter press auditors hold after button office inspections. The pulse is checked, not assumed. Every grove is counted once.
